# Danesh alpha function

`eos.pr_danesh_alpha`

## Equation

$$
\alpha = \left(1 + \tilde m\left(1 - \sqrt{T_r}\right)\right)^2,\qquad \tilde m = \begin{cases}1.21\,m & T_r > 1 \\ m & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}
$$

In the form the library evaluates:

```python
m = 0.37464 + 1.54226*omega - 0.26992*omega**2,  m_mod = 1.21*m above Tr = 1 else m,  alpha = (1 + m_mod*(1 - sqrt(Tr)))**2
```

## Source

**NeqSim master `AttractiveTermPrDanesh`**

`alpha(temperature)`, ported verbatim

DOI: [10.1016/0378-3812(91)80034-S](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-3812(91)80034-S)

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `omega` | dimensionless | the acentric factor |
| `Tr` | dimensionless | the reduced temperature |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | dimensionless | the temperature-dependent alpha function |


## Valid range

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Tr > 0` | raises | the formula takes a square root of `Tr`; zero and below are not states |


## Assumptions

These are **not** checked at runtime. They are what the caller has to
satisfy for the result to mean what it says.


- the 1.21 factor above the critical is NeqSim's, applied to the Peng-Robinson Soave coefficient to damp the attraction past `Tr = 1`.

- the alpha is cubic-agnostic; the `a` and `b` it scales are the cubic's own.




## Worked example

Source: derived from the equation above

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| `omega` | 0.152 |
| `Tr` | 0.7 |

| Output | Expected |
|---|---|
| `alpha` | 1.2066270990034567 |

Relative tolerance: `1e-12`

omega = 0.152, Tr = 0.7: m = 0.37464 + 1.54226*0.152 - 0.26992*0.152**2 = 0.60282728832 m_mod = m (Tr = 0.7 < 1) = 0.60282728832 1 - sqrt(Tr) = 1 - sqrt(0.7) = 0.16333997346592444 alpha = (1 + 0.60282728832*0.16333997346592444)**2 = 1.2066270990034567
